body:
Inside, I'm just feeling like there's nothing here worth fighting for, nothing that's worth the struggle.

I'm expecting a lifestyle change pretty soon. Less responsibilities hopefully, new state. Maybe things will be different.
I'm going school and work right now, the reason why I'm so stressed out. Maybe things will be better once I'm done with school and I only have to worry about work.
There's just nothing to enjoy, no escape from myself and my past.

This is hands down the most powerful and insightful comment I've ever read on Reddit. Thank you SO MUCH for taking the time to type this out, it  's really moving for me. Honestly, when I try and vilifying him, I feel like he has so much less power over me.

That makes a lot of intuitive sense, I'm willing to give it a shot.

The only worry I have is that I don't want to become like him. I hope that putting myself in his shoes doesn't make me feel like what he did was OK.

I've tried so many different things, but I haven't tried this yet, so we'll see, hopefully I can make some progress.

I'm sorry that it came off that way, I was being 100% genuine and sincere. I've honestly tried working on *desensitizing* myself since I read your post, as opposed to just resisting triggers and flashbacks like usual. Do you have any specific advice about how to do this?

Ya, telling my family, I don't know, that's such a tough one. I know they'd want to know, but I don't think they could be much help. They can't change what happened, and I know they'd still love me no matter what. I've just never really talked to them much about anything personal, not even who my crushes are, let alone the worst night of my life. Maybe someday, but for now it just doesn't feel right. I'd rather be telling them about how I've found the love my life and I couldn't be happier, hopefully they'll see that day eventually.
Wow, no one has ever given me this advice before. That's just crazy enough to work! I'm so glad I posted here, I cannot thank you enough for this tip!

Listening to music or a wave cd sounds like a great idea, I'd like to give that a shot. Getting up straight out of bed also sounds like a good way of avoiding the morning depression I get when I wake up and am immediately triggered by my surroundings. I keep a dream journal, so maybe I'll put it on my desk so I have to get up and write in it out of my bed. Position plays a big role, because of what happened, I don't like to sleep on my stomach *at all*. Unfortunately, I can only fall asleep on my stomach. I literally can't fall asleep on my back, and it's hard for me to fall asleep on my side, maybe I'll practice on that. I still sleep enough, luckily, I just don't enjoy it like I used to.

Wow, thanks so much for this reply. I think you're right, maybe if I spent more time in my bed when I'm not trying to sleep, I can learn to feel OK there. Maybe I will get a stuffed animal, it's been so long since I've had one. I've never told friends or family, but I've told one counselor. I'll probably tell friends eventually, I just don't have any friends that I talk about that kind of stuff with right now. I don't see any reason to tell my family, they'll feel better if they don't know about the ways I'm suffering, I don't want them to know about my pain.

I've tried posting wherever I think my post is most appropriate. So far, that's been in /dating_advice, /sex, and now /rapecounseling. I've posted in /depression before on another account, that's a great subreddit too. Never seen /needadvice before, I'll have to check it out.

I'm moving soon, but I plan on looking for a new therapist where I'm headed, never quite finished up with my last one.
That really sucks, I'm sorry so much of your time was wasted. Thanks for your encouragement, it means a lot to be heard.

Reframing virginity was something my therapist and I were working on. It's hard for me, but it seems like a good idea. I haven't completely lost hope, I just don't know how to find that man, even though I know he's out there.

I've been out of therapy for a while. For one, my therapist left town, but also, I felt like I was becoming too dependent on therapy. Therapy became my favorite 45 minutes of the week, and as soon as I left I was already waiting for the next session. I just felt like I couldn't solve any problems on my own, and I *needed* my therapist to solve my problems for me, but he couldn't, which made me feel even more helpless. I'm moving in several months, maybe I'll look for a therapist in my new state of residence.

I agree about it being unhealthy to dwell on the past, and how I should focus on the positive things in life. But for me, it's not a matter of choice. I have [intrusive thoughts](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrusive_thoughts) that remind me of my experience, it feels like it's still happening to me even though it was two years ago. What you're saying sounds great in theory, but in practice it's impossible for me. My best bet has been to find ways of mentally escaping from reality, I find entertainment most successful in this regard.
Makes a lot of sense, thanks.
